index 0000000..536cf4e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/bandit/core/nosec.py
@@ -0,0 +1,445 @@
+#
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""Parsing of the ``# nosec`` family of suppression comments.
+
+Beside the plain ``# nosec`` comment, which suppresses the findings of the
+line it sits on, three directives are understood:
+
+``# nosec-begin [SELECTOR]``
+    Suppress every following line until the matching ``# nosec-end``.
+``# nosec-end``
+    Close the most recently opened region.
+``# nosec-next-line [SELECTOR]``
+    Suppress the statement following the directive.
+
+Every directive takes an optional selector describing which tests it applies
+to. An absent selector suppresses all of them.
+"""
+import collections
+import fnmatch
+import logging
+import re
+import tokenize
+
+from bandit.core import extension_loader
+from bandit.core import utils
+
+LOG = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+NOSEC_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s*nosec:?\s*(?P<tests>[^#]+)?#?")
+NOSEC_COMMENT_TESTS = re.compile(r"(?:(B\d+|[a-z\d_]+),?)+", re.IGNORECASE)
+NOSEC_BEGIN_COMMENT = re.compile(
+    r"#\s*nosec-begin\b:?(?P<tests>[^#]*)", re.IGNORECASE
+)
+NOSEC_END_COMMENT = re.compile(r"#\s*nosec-end\b", re.IGNORECASE)
+NOSEC_NEXT_LINE_COMMENT = re.compile(
+    r"#\s*nosec-next-line\b:?(?P<tests>[^#]*)", re.IGNORECASE
+)
+
+# the kinds of comment understood by _parse_comment()
+NOSEC = "nosec"
+BEGIN = "nosec-begin"
+END = "nosec-end"
+NEXT_LINE = "nosec-next-line"
+
+# tokens of a selector expression, anything else is a syntax error
+SELECTOR_TOKENS = re.compile(r"[\w*?]+|[(),|&!-]|\S")
+SELECTOR_ATOM = re.compile(r"[\w*?]+\Z")
+
+# lines which do not hold a statement of their own and are therefore skipped
+# when looking for the target of a "nosec-next-line" directive
+SKIPPED_LINE = re.compile(r"(?:[(){}\[\];\s]|\.\.\.)*\Z")
+
+# tokens which are not part of the statement they are surrounded by
+NON_STATEMENT_TOKENS = frozenset(
+    (
+        tokenize.COMMENT,
+        tokenize.DEDENT,
+        tokenize.ENCODING,
+        tokenize.ENDMARKER,
+        tokenize.INDENT,
+        tokenize.NL,
+    )
+)
+
+# a region opened by a "nosec-begin" directive; regions opened on an indented
+# line are closed again by the first line indented less than "indent"
+Region = collections.namedtuple("Region", ["indent", "tests"])
+
+
+class SelectorSyntaxError(Exception):
+    """Raised when a selector expression cannot be parsed."""
+
+
+class Selection:
+    """The set of tests selected by a selector expression.
+
+    A blanket selection stands for every test there is, including the ones
+    which may be added to a profile later on, and is therefore tracked
+    separately from the test ids it currently resolves to.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, tests, blanket=False):
+        self.tests = frozenset(tests)
+        self.blanket = blanket
+
+    def __or__(self, other):
+        return Selection(
+            self.tests | other.tests, self.blanket or other.blanket
+        )
+
+    def __and__(self, other):
+        return Selection(
+            self.tests & other.tests, self.blanket and other.blanket
+        )
+
+    def __sub__(self, other):
+        # a selection only stays blanket while nothing is taken away from it
+        removed = other.blanket or other.tests
+        return Selection(self.tests - other.tests, self.blanket and not removed)
+
+
+class SelectorParser:
+    """Recursive descent parser for selector expressions.
+
+    Tokens are unioned when they are merely separated by whitespace or a
+    comma, the ``|``, ``&`` and ``-`` operators combine them explicitly and
+    ``!`` negates against the tests enabled for the run. Precedence follows
+    Python's own set operators, ``|`` binding the loosest and ``!`` the
+    tightest, and parentheses group.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, selector, enabled_tests):
+        self.tokens = SELECTOR_TOKENS.findall(selector)
+        self.enabled_tests = frozenset(enabled_tests)
+        self.pos = 0
+
+    def parse(self):
+        selection = self._union()
+        if self._peek() is not None:
+            raise SelectorSyntaxError(f"unexpected {self._peek()!r}")
+        return selection
+
+    def _peek(self):
+        return self.tokens[self.pos] if self.pos < len(self.tokens) else None
+
+    def _next(self):
+        token = self._peek()
+        self.pos += 1
+        return token
+
+    def _union(self):
+        selection = self._intersection()
+        while True:
+            token = self._peek()
+            if token is None or token == ")":
+                return selection
+            if token in ("|", ","):
+                self._next()
+            # anything else is a union written as plain juxtaposition
+            selection = selection | self._intersection()
+
+    def _intersection(self):
+        selection = self._difference()
+        while self._peek() == "&":
+            self._next()
+            selection = selection & self._difference()
+        return selection
+
+    def _difference(self):
+        selection = self._unary()
+        while self._peek() == "-":
+            self._next()
+            selection = selection - self._unary()
+        return selection
+
+    def _unary(self):
+        if self._peek() == "!":
+            self._next()
+            return self._negate(self._unary())
+        return self._atom()
+
+    def _negate(self, selection):
+        return Selection(
+            self.enabled_tests - selection.tests,
+            blanket=not selection.blanket and not selection.tests,
+        )
+
+    def _atom(self):
+        token = self._next()
+        if token == "(":
+            selection = self._union()
+            if self._next() != ")":
+                raise SelectorSyntaxError("unbalanced parenthesis")
+            return selection
+        if token is None or not SELECTOR_ATOM.match(token):
+            raise SelectorSyntaxError(f"expected a test, got {token!r}")
+        return _resolve_selector_token(token, self.enabled_tests)
+
+
+def parse_selector(selector, enabled_tests):
+    """Resolve the selector of a directive to the tests it suppresses.
+
+    :param selector: the text following the directive keyword, may be empty
+    :param enabled_tests: the ids of all tests enabled for this run
+    :return: None when nothing is suppressed, an empty set for a blanket
+             suppression or the set of ids of the suppressed tests
+    """
+    selector = selector.strip() if selector else ""
+    if not selector:
+        return set()
+
+    try:
+        selection = SelectorParser(selector, enabled_tests).parse()
+    except SelectorSyntaxError as e:
+        LOG.warning(
+            "Selector in comment: %s could not be parsed (%s), falling back "
+            "to a union of its tests",
+            selector,
+            e,
+        )
+        selection = _union_of_tokens(selector, enabled_tests)
+
+    if selection.blanket:
+        return set()
+    # an expression selecting no test at all suppresses nothing, as opposed
+    # to a blanket suppression which is also carried by an empty set
+    return set(selection.tests) or None
+
+
+def build_nosec_lines(fdata, enabled_tests=None):
+    """Collect the suppressions of a file, line by line.
+
+    :param fdata: file object with the contents of the file being scanned
+    :param enabled_tests: the ids of all tests enabled for this run
+    :return: dict of line number to the set of ids of the tests suppressed on
+             that line, an empty set standing for a blanket suppression
+    """
+    enabled_tests = frozenset(enabled_tests or ())
+    tokens, lines = _tokenize(fdata)
+
+    directives = {}
+    for token in tokens:
+        if token.type == tokenize.COMMENT:
+            directives[token.start[0]] = _parse_comment(
+                token.string, enabled_tests
+            )
+
+    nosec_lines = _collect_regions(lines, directives)
+    _apply_next_line(nosec_lines, lines, directives, _statements(tokens))
+    return nosec_lines
+
+
+def _collect_regions(lines, directives):
+    """Suppress the lines covered by a region or by a plain nosec comment."""
+    nosec_lines = {}
+    regions = []
+
+    for lineno, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
+        indent = _indentation(line)
+        if indent is not None:
+            # an indented region ends where the indentation it was opened at
+            # is left again
+            regions = [
+                region
+                for region in regions
+                if region.indent is None or indent >= region.indent
+            ]
+
+        kind, tests = directives.get(lineno, (None, None))
+        if kind == END and regions:
+            regions.pop()
+
+        # the line a region is opened on is not part of it yet, which is why
+        # the directive is only pushed once the line has been dealt with
+        suppressed = None
+        for region in regions:
+            suppressed = utils.merge_nosec_tests(suppressed, region.tests)
+        if kind == NOSEC:
+            suppressed = utils.merge_nosec_tests(suppressed, tests)
+        if suppressed is not None:
+            nosec_lines[lineno] = suppressed
+
+        if kind == BEGIN:
+            regions.append(Region(indent or None, tests))
+
+    return nosec_lines
+
+
+def _apply_next_line(nosec_lines, lines, directives, statements):
+    """Suppress the statement following every "nosec-next-line" directive."""
+    for lineno, (kind, tests) in sorted(directives.items()):
+        if kind != NEXT_LINE or tests is None:
+            continue
+        target = _next_statement_line(lines, lineno)
+        if target is None:
+            continue
+        # suppressions are statement wide, so the whole statement the target
+        # line belongs to is covered
+        first, last = statements.get(target, (target, target))
+        for line in range(first, last + 1):
+            nosec_lines[line] = utils.merge_nosec_tests(
+                nosec_lines.get(line), tests
+            )
+
+
+def _parse_comment(comment, enabled_tests):
+    """Determine which kind of suppression a comment holds, if any.
+
+    :param comment: the text of the comment, starting with its "#"
+    :param enabled_tests: the ids of all tests enabled for this run
+    :return: tuple of the kind of the comment and the tests it suppresses
+    """
+    match = NOSEC_NEXT_LINE_COMMENT.search(comment)
+    if match:
+        return NEXT_LINE, parse_selector(match.group("tests"), enabled_tests)
+
+    match = NOSEC_BEGIN_COMMENT.search(comment)
+    if match:
+        return BEGIN, parse_selector(match.group("tests"), enabled_tests)
+
+    if NOSEC_END_COMMENT.search(comment):
+        # anything trailing a "nosec-end" is ignored
+        return END, None
+
+    return NOSEC, _parse_nosec_comment(comment)
+
+
+def _parse_nosec_comment(comment):
+    found_no_sec_comment = NOSEC_COMMENT.search(comment)
+    if not found_no_sec_comment:
+        # there was no nosec comment
+        return None
+
+    matches = found_no_sec_comment.groupdict()
+    nosec_tests = matches.get("tests", set())
+
+    # empty set indicates that there was a nosec comment without specific
+    # test ids or names
+    test_ids = set()
+    if nosec_tests:
+        extman = extension_loader.MANAGER
+        # lookup tests by short code or name
+        for test in NOSEC_COMMENT_TESTS.finditer(nosec_tests):
+            test_match = test.group(1)
+            test_id = _find_test_id_from_nosec_string(extman, test_match)
+            if test_id:
+                test_ids.add(test_id)
+
+    # the comment sits on the line it suppresses, so each of its tests was
+    # named for that very line
+    return utils.NosecTests(test_ids, named=test_ids)
+
+
+def _find_test_id_from_nosec_string(extman, match):
+    test_id = extman.check_id(match)
+    if test_id:
+        return match
+    # Finding by short_id didn't work, let's check the test name
+    test_id = extman.get_test_id(match)
+    if not test_id:
+        # Name and short id didn't work:
+        LOG.warning(
+            "Test in comment: %s is not a test name or id, ignoring", match
+        )
+    return test_id  # We want to return None or the string here regardless
+
+
+def _resolve_selector_token(token, enabled_tests):
+    """Resolve a single test of a selector expression."""
+    keyword = token.lower()
+    if keyword == "all":
+        return Selection(enabled_tests, blanket=True)
+    if keyword == "none":
+        return Selection(())
+
+    if "*" in token or "?" in token:
+        # test ids, and only those, may be globbed
+        pattern = token.upper()
+        matched = {
+            test
+            for test in enabled_tests
+            if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(test, pattern)
+        }
+        if not matched:
+            LOG.warning(
+                "Test in comment: %s does not match any test id, ignoring",
+                token,
+            )
+        return Selection(matched)
+
+    test_id = _find_test_id_from_nosec_string(extension_loader.MANAGER, token)
+    return Selection({test_id} if test_id else ())
+
+
+def _union_of_tokens(selector, enabled_tests):
+    """Union every test of an expression which could not be parsed."""
+    selection = Selection(())
+    for token in re.split(r"[,\s]+", selector):
+        if token:
+            selection = selection | _resolve_selector_token(
+                token, enabled_tests
+            )
+    return selection
+
+
+def _tokenize(fdata):
+    """Tokenize a file, returning its tokens along with its lines.
+
+    A file which cannot be tokenized entirely, because it ends in the middle
+    of a statement, still yields the tokens gathered up to that point.
+    """
+    fdata.seek(0)
+    encoding = "utf-8"
+    tokens = []
+    try:
+        for token in tokenize.tokenize(fdata.readline):
+            if token.type == tokenize.ENCODING:
+                encoding = token.string
+            tokens.append(token)
+    except tokenize.TokenError:
+        pass
+
+    fdata.seek(0)
+    lines = fdata.read().decode(encoding, "replace").splitlines()
+    return tokens, lines
+
+
+def _statements(tokens):
+    """Map every line of a file to the statement it belongs to.
+
+    :param tokens: the tokens of the file
+    :return: dict of line number to the first and last line of its statement
+    """
+    statements = {}
+    first = last = None
+
+    for token in tokens:
+        if token.type == tokenize.NEWLINE:
+            if first is not None:
+                for lineno in range(first, last + 1):
+                    statements[lineno] = (first, last)
+            first = last = None
+        elif token.type in NON_STATEMENT_TOKENS:
+            continue
+        elif first is None:
+            first, last = token.start[0], token.end[0]
+        else:
+            last = max(last, token.end[0])
+
+    return statements
+
+
+def _next_statement_line(lines, lineno):
+    """Find the line holding the statement following a directive."""
+    for index in range(lineno, len(lines)):
+        if not SKIPPED_LINE.match(lines[index].split("#", 1)[0]):
+            return index + 1
+    return None
+
+
+def _indentation(line):
+    """Measure the leading whitespace of a line, None if it holds none."""
+    expanded = line.expandtabs()
+    stripped = expanded.lstrip()
+    return len(expanded) - len(stripped) if stripped else None

+class NosecTests(set):
+    """The ids of the tests suppressed on a line.
+
+    An empty set is a blanket suppression covering every test. The ids a
+    comment spells out on the line itself are remembered separately, as only
+    those are worth reporting when they end up suppressing nothing.
+    """
+
+    def __init__(self, tests=(), named=()):
+        super().__init__(tests)
+        self.named = frozenset(named)
+
+
+def nosec_named_tests(tests):
+    """Get the tests a nosec comment named, out of the ones it suppresses.
+
+    :param tests: set of suppressed test ids
+    :return: the set of test ids the comment named itself
+    """
+    return getattr(tests, "named", frozenset())
+
+
+def merge_nosec_tests(tests, other):
+    """Combine two sets of tests suppressed by a nosec comment.
+
+    None stands for the absence of any suppression, while an empty set is a
+    blanket suppression of every test and dominates specific ones.
+
+    :param tests: set of suppressed test ids, or None
+    :param other: set of suppressed test ids, or None
+    :return: the combined set of suppressed test ids, or None
+    """
+    if tests is None:
+        return other
+    if other is None:
+        return tests
+    if not tests or not other:
+        return set()
+    return NosecTests(
+        set(tests) | set(other),
+        nosec_named_tests(tests) | nosec_named_tests(other),
+    )
+
+
 def get_nosec(nosec_lines, context):

     for lineno in context["linerange"]:
-        nosec = nosec_lines.get(lineno, None)
-        if nosec is not None:
-            return nosec
-    return None
+        nosec = merge_nosec_tests(nosec, nosec_lines.get(lineno, None))
+        if nosec is not None and not nosec:
+            # a blanket suppression cannot be widened any further

+    return nosec
